description: if true then 1 else "a" end: Ty.joinTy has no *structural* case for (Int, an instance of String), but this is exactly the situation Ty.union exists for -- union(Int, an instance of String) is already expressible in the current grammar (see Ty.union's own docstring: currently inert on the checker path). No language gap -- what is missing is a joinTy that produces a union instead of answering none, so the if' rule can infer this type rather than reject it.
